messages:
rachel: Heads-up: we9re enforcing org SSO + OIDC-only CI credentials and enabling runnerless (hosted) runners by default next Wed 2026-06-02. Window: 00:00 -> 06:00 UTC. Please review if you maintain self-hosted runner fleets.

jess: Short summary for teams: 1) GitHub accounts must be provisioned via Okta SSO (org enforced), 2) CI workflows must use OIDC tokens or the new ci-auth action, 3) self-hosted runners will be opt-in only post-cutover.

tom: Will SSH keys or long-lived deploy tokens stop working?

rachel: Yes 3 deploy tokens and static keys will be rejected for workflow auth. We provide a short-lived proxy for partner CI for 14 days. If you rely on a long-lived token, file an exception with Security.

ci-tooling: Example migration snippet (GH action):
```
- name: Get OIDC
  id: oidc
  uses: redwood/get-oidc-token@v1
- name: Authenticate
  uses: redwood/ci-auth@v2
  with:
    oidc-token: ${{ steps.oidc.outputs.token }}
```

jess: Canary plan: infra repos -> ops tools -> customer-facing. First canary 02:30 UTC with infra/infra-ctl, monitor 45m.

idp-bot: NOTICE: Okta SSO enforcement scheduled for 2026-06-02T00:00Z. Users not signed in will be blocked from pushes that require SSO.

rachel: Action items for owners: 1) disable runner-local secrets in workflows, 2) swap to ci-auth or OIDC, 3) if using self-hosted runners, register them under the new runner-manager and request opt-in by EOD Mon 2026-06-01.

tom: How do we handle third-party bots (e.g., release bots) that can9t do OIDC?

jess: We9ll issue short-lived service certs via the service-account portal and create a managed token for 14 days. Long-term: onboard to the broker.

infra-oncall: Rollback knobs: org flag to allow legacy tokens for 2h, and we can re-open runner registration. Use infra-oncall for emergency reverts.

rachel: I9ll post the migration checklist + repo scan results in #devex later today. If you need help scanning repos, ping @jess and we9ll run a sweep. :mag:
